Manual for Trawl v0.9.4. Build identity.

HTTP API

trawld serves a JSON API over HTTPS under the base path /api/v1. Request bodies are JSON and carry Content-Type: application/json. Responses are JSON unless a route says otherwise. The Prometheus scrape route, /metrics, sits outside the base path.

The examples on this page follow the same convention as health checks: TRAWL_URL names the HTTPS API and TRAWL_CURL_CONFIG names an owner-only curl config file that holds the Authorization header. Keep a key in a curl config file shows how to write it.

Authentication

Section titled “Authentication”

Every route under /api/v1 except /api/v1/health requires a bearer token:

Keys and the roles that carry permissions are created with fleet-admin. See access administration.

Status Code When
401 auth_error The header is missing or malformed, or the key is invalid, expired, or revoked. The response does not say which.
403 forbidden The key is valid but holds no permission that trawld recognizes. The message is no trawl grant for this key.
403 forbidden The key is valid but lacks the permission the route checks. The message is insufficient permissions.
503 service_unavailable The keystore did not answer. The message is auth backend unavailable.

Roles and permissions

Section titled “Roles and permissions”

A role is a named bundle of permission strings in the Fleet keystore. A key can hold any number of roles, and its permissions are the union of those roles. trawld checks permissions, never role names. A permission string it does not recognize grants nothing. These are the permissions in the trawl namespace:

Permission Allows
query Run queries, capture results and read the key’s own captured results, list running queries, and read or clear the key’s query history
schema_read Read the schema, the field catalog, conflict samples, and repin status
validate Validate DSL without running it
saved_query Create, read, update, and delete saved queries, schedules, and report runs
export Export query results
stream Subscribe to live event streams
query_cancel Cancel the key’s own running queries
server_manage Read server stats and the dashboard, preview ingest, cancel any query, and see the text of system-owned retained work
ingest Submit events to /api/v1/ingest
schema_write Repin a field, read a repin job the key requested by its id, reclaim pins, and acknowledge degraded pins
investigation_read With query, list and read every investigation in the installation, with its steps, findings, and kept evidence
investigation_write With query and investigation_read, create investigations, attach searches and correlation reads, keep rows, record findings and notes, and close or reopen any investigation

schema_read exposes samples of event values in conflict evidence: up to 5 values per conflict row, each cut to 256 bytes.

Conventions

Section titled “Conventions”

Error envelope

Section titled “Error envelope”

Every error that trawld itself produces has this body:

Field Type Description
code string One of the codes below
message string Human-readable summary
details array Present for parse_error and validation_error. Each entry has message and optional span, label and hint. A span holds byte offsets into the query text. A parse_error entry always has one. A validation_error entry has none, and a validation_error that trawld finds only while it runs the query, such as a timechart over a column that is not a timestamp, has no entries.
conflict object Present for sequence_conflict only: expected, the expected_seq the request carried, and current, the investigation’s seq now. See investigations
Code Status Meaning
parse_error 400 The DSL does not parse
validation_error 400 The DSL parses but fails semantic checks: unknown function, wrong arity, or a pipeline over the expression budget or stage cap
result_too_large 400 The result exceeded max_result_rows, or an aggregation after a Rust stage such as extract kv would drop input at a cap. The message names the cap and its limit. See stream live events for the caps. A capture also answers it when a whole result does not fit the capture’s caps. See shapes and caps
bad_request 400 Malformed input. Also the code on a 409 that has no code of its own.
capture_source_too_large 400 A capture’s window selects more stored data than [capture] source_max_bytes. Nothing was scanned. Narrow the window. See admission
focus_incomplete 400 A context read’s focus row has no usable _time, or no text value for a key its scope names. The read is never widened
focus_ambiguous 400 A context read’s focus capture has two columns of a name the read needs
windows_overlap 400 A compare request’s two windows overlap. The message names both
correlation_invalid 400 A correlation read’s input cannot be built into a query, such as a compare filter with a pipe stage. The message names the input
ingest_error 400, 413 An ingest body that cannot be read. 413 when a gzip body decodes past [ingest] max_body_bytes
ingest_batch_too_large 413 An ingest request holds more events or bytes than external producers may place in the hot buffer, so it can never be admitted
request_too_large 413 A request body exceeds the router’s body limit, [server] max_request_body_bytes or [ingest] max_body_bytes. The message names the setting and its value. See body size limits. Through trawl-web, also the proxy’s own refusal of a body over [server] max_request_body_bytes, over the proxy body budget of 128 MiB when that setting is above it, or, under /api/auth/*, over the login body limit of 16 KiB, before trawld is contacted. The message names the limit in the same words
preview_too_large 413 An ingest preview sample holds more than 500 events
unsupported_encoding 415 An ingest preview body carries a Content-Encoding other than identity
auth_error 401 Authentication failed
forbidden 403 The key lacks a permission
not_found 404 No such resource, or the key does not own it. The response does not say which.
result_unavailable 409 A captured result’s record exists, but its file is missing. See captured result outcomes
sequence_conflict 409 An overwrite of an investigation carried an expected_seq that is no longer its seq. The envelope’s conflict member holds expected and current. See investigations
investigation_exists 409 A create named an investigation id that exists with another creator or other fields
investigation_closed 409 The investigation is closed and takes nothing new until a writer reopens it
evidence_budget_exceeded 409 Keeping a result would take an investigation’s or the installation’s evidence over its budget. Not a 429: evidence frees only as it ages out or when an operator deletes an investigation. See attach a capture
result_gone 410 A captured result expired, was pruned to fit a lowered quota, or its investigation’s evidence retention ended or the investigation was deleted. The message says which. See captured result outcomes
rate_limited 429 The key’s per-minute bucket is empty. Sent with Retry-After
too_many_streams 429 max_sse_connections reached
capture_busy 429 The key’s capture queue is full, the installation runs as many captures as it may, or the deadline passed during admission. For an attached capture or a keep or finding that keeps a result, that includes waiting for a database connection, a lock, or an answer from the database. Sent with Retry-After. See admission
capture_quota_exceeded 429 The key’s or the installation’s capture quota has no room for one more result. Sent with Retry-After. See admission
execution_error 500 DuckDB failed for a reason other than its resource budgets, or the query was cancelled. Details are logged, never returned.
execution_error 400 A result cell is an integer outside the signed and unsigned 64-bit range. The message names the column. See Result columns.
result_corrupt 500 A captured result’s file does not match its recorded digest. See captured result outcomes
internal_error 500 Anything else
timeout 504 The query started but did not finish within timeout_secs. Through trawl-web, also the proxy’s own 504 when trawld’s response head did not arrive within timeout_secs plus 10 s; the message says trawld may still be running the work. Open streams and bodies in flight are never cut
timeout 408 trawl-web only: the request body did not arrive whole within 30 s. The request was not sent to trawld
service_unavailable 503 A dependency is down, the server is at capacity, or the node cannot serve the route
hot_buffer_full 503 The hot buffer has no room for an ingest request. Sent with Retry-After
request_limit_reached 503 trawld is at its [server] max_concurrent_requests limit, or a health or /metrics request is at the probe allowance (fixed at 3), or a query list or cancel request is at the control allowance (fixed at 4). The handler did not run and nothing was ingested. No Retry-After. Retry with backoff. See the request limit. Through trawl-web, also the proxy’s own refusal when it is at its request count (fixed at 64, /healthz excepted) or when its budget for buffered request bodies (fixed at 128 MiB) cannot cover the request’s declared body; the message names trawl-web as the hop and the request was not sent to trawld
corpus_recovering 503 The server cannot yet count every stored event exactly once, so it refuses the read. No Retry-After. See corpus recovering
query_resource_exhausted 503 The query needed more spill or memory than the query database may use, or more regex memory than trawld’s regex bounds allow, or no query preparation slot came free before its deadline. No Retry-After. See query resource exhausted

Corpus recovering

Section titled “Corpus recovering”

A read answers 503 corpus_recovering while the corpus is unsettled: after a restart, until compaction proves that the WAL from before the restart is covered, or while a daily rollup marker is unfinished. It applies to queries, captures of the corpus, exports, uncached field values, manual runs, and repins. The message is fixed for each reason and names no count, path, or marker:

Reason Message
restart_backlog Search is unavailable while the server finishes loading data from before its restart.
rollup_pending Search is unavailable while the server finishes an interrupted storage rollup.

When both reasons hold, the response names rollup_pending. The reason is the cause_kind of the http_failure event, and checks.corpus in server health names it too. The envelope carries no reason field. Live tail, | from saved queries, /api/v1/schema, /api/v1/schema/services, health, metrics, and a cached field-values hit answer as usual. See reads while the corpus is unsettled.

trawld checks the key and the route’s permission before it reads a byte of the body. A missing or bad key gets 401 and a key without the permission gets 403, whatever the body holds. trawld sends that refusal without waiting for the body, and hangs up without reading the rest of it. A client that is still sending the body when the refusal comes can see the connection close or reset instead of the response. trawld reads a body only when its key may use the route, and reads it under the size limit: a body over the limit is refused with 413 and the envelope, code request_too_large. After the same checks, a JSON body that cannot be read gets 400 with the envelope, code bad_request. That covers a body sent without Content-Type: application/json, a body that is not valid JSON, and JSON that does not match the request shape. No route answers with the HTTP framework’s own 415 or 422.

Every response carries an X-Request-Id header holding a ULID. Quote it when reporting a problem. The trawl CLI and trawl-client end the message of every error that got a response with (request <id>).

Query resource exhausted

Section titled “Query resource exhausted”

A query, export, or field sample answers 503 query_resource_exhausted when it needs more spill or memory than the query database may use: more than [server] query_spill_max_bytes of spill, or more than [server] query_memory_limit of memory. DuckDB reports both limits with one error type, so the response does not say which one ran out. The body is fixed:

The message names no path, size, or DuckDB text. The response carries no Retry-After. The status is 503, not 500, because nothing is broken, and not a 4xx, because every query shares the budgets: the same query can finish on an idle server and fail beside a heavy one. Narrow the time range, add a filter, or drop a wide stats ... by before you retry. The server keeps serving, and a small query on the same server succeeds.

The http_failure event records error_class=service_unavailable and cause_kind=duckdb_resource_exhausted. A query that timed out first keeps its 504 timeout, even when DuckDB then fails with the same error. The rule covers planning, execution, row fetch, and export. See query scratch and budgets for the settings and diagnose a 503 or 504 from a query for the operator steps.

A query, export, or live stream also answers this 503 when its regex work does not fit trawld’s regex memory bounds. The body, the message, and the missing Retry-After are the same. The http_failure event records error_class=service_unavailable and one of two cause kinds:

cause_kind Meaning
regex_budget_exhausted The query needs more regex memory than one query may hold, so it can never run as written. Its patterns’ compiled state is over the 32 MiB budget a query has, or its patterns and its batch RE2 allowance together are over the 512 MiB one query may hold of the regex reservation.
regex_reservation_exhausted The query fits on its own, but the 1.25 GiB regex reservation the whole server shares is held by other queries and live streams now. The same query can run when they finish.

A request that takes query text also answers this 503 when no query preparation slot came free before its deadline. That covers /query, export, /api/v1/validate, a live stream’s setup, saved-query create and update, and captures. The message is trawld is at its query preparation allowance; the query was not started; retry later with backoff, and there is no Retry-After. The http_failure event records error_class=service_unavailable and this cause kind:

cause_kind Meaning
preparation_allowance_exhausted Every query preparation slot stayed in use until the request’s deadline, so the query was never parsed. The allowance is half the cores, at least 2 and at most max_concurrent_queries, with no config key. Retry with backoff. See preparation off the reactor.

The bounds are fixed constants, with no config key. A batch query holds an RE2 allowance for each regex call DuckDB binds or runs, every copy included, on each query thread: 6.88 MiB for a matches operand or a search /regex/, 13.38 MiB for an extract, and 9 KiB for each regex call trawld writes itself to read a severity. One sev() is 41 such calls, and reading a field pinned to SEVERITY from the hot buffer is 199. A filter over both the hot buffer and stored data runs in each, but a query thread reads one of them at a time, so its patterns count once. A glob, like, or ilike operand never reaches RE2. Use fewer or simpler patterns, or retry later. /api/v1/validate takes no share of the regex reservation and never answers with the regex causes. It builds each pattern to check it and keeps nothing afterwards, so a validation in progress uses at most 4 MiB while a pattern builds. See the memory arithmetic for how the reservation sits in the process’s memory.

Rate limiting

Section titled “Rate limiting”

trawld keeps one token bucket per API key and route class. The bucket refills continuously and holds one minute of requests, so a burst of up to the full per-minute quota passes before the first 429.

Route class Config key Default Applies to
Interactive [server.rate_limit] default_rpm 100 Every authenticated route except /api/v1/ingest
Ingest [server.rate_limit] ingest_rpm 1000 /api/v1/ingest, for a key that holds ingest

A key without ingest spends its interactive bucket when it posts to /api/v1/ingest. A 0 disables the class. When any of the key’s roles sets rate_rpm, the largest such value replaces the class default in both classes. The 429 body is the error envelope with code rate_limited. It carries Retry-After: the seconds until the bucket holds a token again, rounded up, and never less than 1. No response carries X-RateLimit-* headers. Three other responses carry Retry-After: 503 hot_buffer_full from ingest, and 429 capture_busy and capture_quota_exceeded from captures. /api/v1/health and /metrics are not rate limited.

Pagination

Section titled “Pagination”

Query results page with limit and offset in the request. The response echoes them in pagination with returned, the number of rows in this page, and total, the number of rows the execution produced before the page was cut from them. History and run listings take limit and offset as query parameters and return total. Catalog listings take limit and return truncated. The field detail route pages its service rows with an opaque services_cursor.

Result columns

Section titled “Result columns”

A result is columns and rows. The query response, a report run’s result, and the stream’s data and snapshot frames all carry one. Each column is an object with a name and a required type:

type comes from a closed set: boolean, integer, float, string, timestamp, date, time, list, and mixed. A list column also has items, the type of its elements, in the same object shape. A client must refuse a column whose type it does not know. The type comes from execution, not from the catalog, so a zero-row result is typed too.

Each cell is encoded under its column’s type. A null cell is JSON null under every type.

type Cell
boolean true or false
integer A decimal string, for example "9007199254740993"
float A JSON number, or one of the strings "NaN", "Infinity" and "-Infinity"
string A string
timestamp RFC 3339 with six fraction digits and an explicit offset, for example "2026-10-22T12:34:56.123456Z", or "infinity" or "-infinity"
date YYYY-MM-DD, for example "2026-10-22"
time HH:MM:SS, with a fraction when it has one, for example "12:34:56.123456"
list An array of cells, each encoded under items
mixed An object that tags the cell with its own type, for example {"type": "integer", "value": "200"}

An integer cell is a string so that a JavaScript client keeps every digit past 2^53. The spelling is canonical: -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*). A decimal string has no plus sign, no leading zero, no -0, and no whitespace. The value is in the signed or the unsigned 64-bit range, from -9223372036854775808 to 18446744073709551615. A decoder refuses any other spelling and any value outside that range. It also refuses a JSON number under integer, and a string under float other than the three spellings in the table. A query whose result has an integer outside the range, for example a sum past 18446744073709551615, is refused with 400 execution_error. The message names the column. Cast the column with tonumber() or tostring().

A timestamp cell uses Z at offset zero and +HH:MM or -HH:MM otherwise. A query response writes timestamps in the request’s timezone. Report runs and stream frames write them in UTC. A year outside 0000 to 9999 uses the ISO 8601 expanded form, a sign and at least four digits, for example +10000-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z. infinity and -infinity are DuckDB’s infinite timestamps.

A mixed column holds cells of more than one type. Only a column that an extract kv stage computes, or a merge of live frames, can be mixed. Each non-null cell carries its own type and value, and a list tag also carries items. A decoder reads the cell from its tag, never from its spelling.

A column with no evidence of its type is string. That is an all-null column that a stage after extract kv computes, such as let x = null, or a field that is null in a live data frame. A column that a stage after extract kv passes on from its input, renamed or not, takes the input column’s type when its own cells give no evidence, so a result with no rows left still has typed columns. When you merge live frames, treat an all-null string column as no evidence.

These limits apply:

  • DuckDB DECIMAL, INTERVAL, STRUCT, MAP, and UNION values arrive as null cells in a string column.
  • A timestamp that a stage after extract kv computes is written in UTC, not in the request’s timezone.
  • A date or time column that passes through a stage after extract kv is string.
  • A mixed column tags a timestamp that a stage after extract kv computes as string, on its own or as a list item. A column whose every cell is such a timestamp is timestamp.

The schema routes keep DuckDB type names, such as BIGINT and VARCHAR. The lowercase type vocabulary is for result columns only.

Timestamps

Section titled “Timestamps”

Every instant is RFC 3339 in UTC, except result cells, which Result columns describes. Catalog, repin, pin reclamation, schedule window, and captured result instants carry microseconds and a Z suffix, for example 2026-08-01T10:00:00.000000Z. History, saved query, schedule created_at and updated_at, and run started_at and finished_at carry a +00:00 offset, for example 2026-03-14T02:00:00+00:00.

Body size limits

Section titled “Body size limits”
Config key Default Applies to
[server] max_request_body_bytes "128K" Every route except /api/v1/ingest
[ingest] max_body_bytes "16M" /api/v1/ingest

Both accept sizes such as "128K" and "1M". These two keys are the only body bounds. A body over the limit is refused with 413 request_too_large, whether Content-Length announced the size or trawld found it while reading a chunked body. The message names the setting and its value, for example request body exceeds [server] max_request_body_bytes (131072 bytes). trawld hangs up on an oversized body and does not read the rest of it. While trawld is at its request limit, the 503 request_limit_reached comes before the 413. A client that is still uploading can lose the 413 to a connection reset. The trawl CLI and client then report network error: the server closed the connection before the upload finished; the request may exceed the server's request size limit, or the server may be at its request limit. A gzip ingest body is held to [ingest] max_body_bytes twice: once as sent, and once decoded. trawld stops decoding one byte past the limit and answers 413 ingest_error.

Query timeout

Section titled “Query timeout”

[server] timeout_secs (default 30) is one absolute deadline per request, started after authentication. Queue waits, from saved resolution, and execution all spend from it. If the deadline passes before the query starts, the response is 503 service_unavailable with the message server at capacity: the query was not started. If it passes after the query starts, the response is 504 timeout. The deadline applies to /api/v1/query, /api/v1/export, and /api/v1/schema/values/{field}. A capture has a shorter deadline of its own, [capture] deadline_secs, which timeout_secs caps. See admission and quotas.

CORS

Section titled “CORS”

trawld sends CORS headers only when [server] cors_allowed_origins is not empty. It then allows GET and POST with the Authorization and Content-Type headers from the listed origins.

Health

Section titled “Health”

Server health

Section titled “Server health”

GET /api/v1/health

Permission: none. The route is unauthenticated.

Reports the query engine’s latest sample, and probes the Fleet keystore, the app-state store, and the data directory. The duckdb check reads a sample that trawld takes on its own schedule, so a health request never waits for the engine and never takes an executor permit.

Request

Response

Field Type Description
status string ok when every check passes. degraded when duckdb reads slow, auth_db, storage_db, or data_path reads error, ingest_capacity reads refusing, or corpus reads anything but ok. unavailable when duckdb reads error.
checks object Exactly six keys. duckdb is ok, slow, or error. auth_db, storage_db, and data_path are each ok or error. ingest_capacity is ok or refusing. corpus is ok, rollup_pending, or restart_backlog. No diagnostics or paths.
version string The trawld package version

degraded does not prove that authenticated requests can run. An auth_db failure turns every authenticated route into a 503.

duckdb reads the latest engine sample. Every 10 seconds, a dedicated thread runs SELECT 1 on a connection of its own to the query database, with a 250 ms budget. A sample that runs past the budget is interrupted, and no new sample starts until it returns.

duckdb Meaning status HTTP
ok The latest sample succeeded within its budget ok unless another check differs 200
slow The latest sample ran past its budget or failed with Out of Memory, and a sample succeeded in the last 60 seconds degraded 200
error The latest sample returned any other DuckDB error, no sample has succeeded in the last 60 seconds, or none has succeeded since boot unavailable 503

A busy engine does not turn the check to error while a sample has succeeded in the last 60 seconds. A full executor pool, permits held after a timeout, and live streams do not change duckdb or status, because the sample uses no permit. The sample shares the query memory and spill budgets, so queries that exhaust them can make it read slow. Read saturation from trawl_query_permits_in_use and trawl_query_pool_size on /metrics. The response adds no sample age or diagnostics; trawl_engine_sample_age_seconds reports the age.

ingest_capacity reads refusing while the hot buffer refuses ingest for lack of space, and ok otherwise, including on a node with ingest disabled. Reads keep working while it refuses, so the response stays 200 and probes do not restart the server. See hot-buffer admission.

corpus names why corpus reads answer 503 corpus_recovering, and reads ok when they do not. rollup_pending wins when both reasons hold. The state clears without a restart, so the response stays 200. A query-only node never reads restart_backlog. See reads while the corpus is unsettled.

Errors

Status Code When
503 none status is unavailable. The body is the health response, not the error envelope.

Query

Section titled “Query”

Run a query

Section titled “Run a query”

POST /api/v1/query

Permission: query

Runs a DSL query and returns one page of rows. A query whose first stage is from saved reads a stored report run instead of the corpus.

Parameters

Name In Type Required Description
query body string yes The DSL query
limit body integer no Rows per page. Default and cap: [server] max_result_rows (100000).
offset body integer no Rows to skip. Default 0. offset + limit may not exceed max_result_rows.
timezone body string no Timestamp display zone: "UTC", "local", or a fixed offset such as "+05:30". Default "UTC".

Request

Response

Field Type Description
columns array The columns in result order, each with its name and type. See Result columns.
rows array One array per row, one cell per column, each encoded under its column’s type
pagination object limit, offset, returned, and total for this page
pagination.total integer Rows this execution produced, before the response window was cut from them. Compare it with returned to tell a whole result from a page of one.
execution object Optional execution metadata. Present on successful server query responses, including zero-row results. Absent on synthetic client results.
execution.started_at string Server start instant in RFC 3339 UTC, with a Z suffix. Independent of the request’s timezone.
execution.duration_ms integer Server-measured duration in milliseconds. Zero is valid.
degraded_fields array Fields the query bound whose pin is degraded, including fields filtered on and then projected away. Absent when empty. Stale by at most schema_cache_ttl_secs.
severity_columns array Result columns that hold OTel severity numbers other than _severity. Absent when empty.

The server captures execution.started_at beside its monotonic timer. The duration includes admission and execution within that timed section. It excludes subsequent history processing, response serialization, and browser transit. Each page request has its own execution metadata.

Errors

Status Code When
400 parse_error The DSL does not parse
400 validation_error Unknown function, wrong arity, or a pipeline over the expression budget or stage cap
400 bad_request timezone is not UTC, local, or a fixed offset, or offset + limit exceeds max_result_rows
400 result_too_large The result exceeded max_result_rows, or an aggregation after a Rust stage such as extract kv would drop input at its group, distinct-value or exact-value cap. The message names the cap and its limit.
400 execution_error A result cell is an integer outside the signed and unsigned 64-bit range. The message names the column.
404 not_found A from saved stage names a saved query the key does not own, or one with no successful run
409 bad_request A from saved stage selects a run that has columns but no Parquet file. The message names the run route.
500 execution_error DuckDB failed or the query was cancelled
503 query_resource_exhausted The query went over the spill or memory budget. See query resource exhausted.
503 service_unavailable The deadline passed before the query started, or a cold file moved during the read. Retry.
503 service_unavailable The hot buffer’s snapshot could not be built. The message is recent events could not be read for this query.
503 corpus_recovering The corpus is unsettled. See corpus recovering.
504 timeout The deadline passed after the query started

Validate

Section titled “Validate”

Validate a query

Section titled “Validate a query”

POST /api/v1/validate

Permission: validate

Parses and checks a DSL query without running it. Field names are not checked against the schema.

Parameters

Name In Type Required Description
query body string yes The DSL query

Request

Response

A valid query whose formatting is refused carries no formatted text:

Field Type Description
valid boolean Whether the query parsed and passed semantic checks
errors array Error details in the envelope’s details shape. Empty when valid.
formatted string The query in canonical formatting, checked to read back as the same query. Present only when valid and format_error is absent.
format_error object Why a valid query has no formatted text. Absent otherwise.
format_error.kind string too_long: the formatted text would pass the 65,536-byte query limit, for example because escaping grew a quoted string. unfaithful: the formatter could not write text that reads back as the same query.
format_error.message string The reason, for a person

An invalid query is a 200 with valid: false. A pipeline over the expression budget reports as invalid here rather than as a 400. A format refusal is not an error: the query is still valid and runs, and the refusal never appears in errors.

Errors

Status Code When
none No errors beyond Authentication and Rate limiting

Export

Section titled “Export”

Export query results

Section titled “Export query results”

POST /api/v1/export

Permission: export

Runs a query and returns the rows as a file. Timestamps are UTC. The row cap is [server] max_export_rows (1000000) instead of max_result_rows. Rows past the cap are dropped; the export is not refused.

Parameters

Name In Type Required Description
format query string no csv, json, or parquet. Default csv.
query body string yes The DSL query
limit body integer no Row cap. Default and maximum: max_export_rows.

Request

Response

The body is the file. The headers name its type:

format Content-Type Content-Disposition
csv text/csv; charset=utf-8 attachment; filename="export.csv"
json application/x-ndjson attachment; filename="export.ndjson"
parquet application/vnd.apache.parquet attachment; filename="export.parquet"

An export file is not the result wire. Each format keeps its own conventions:

  • json writes one object per row. Integers are JSON numbers with every digit. A float that is not finite is null. Timestamps are RFC 3339 text.
  • csv writes every cell as text. Integers keep every digit.
  • parquet keeps DuckDB’s column types. A stored BIGINT past 2^53 exports exactly. DuckDB writes a HUGEINT column as DOUBLE, which is exact only up to 2^53. A sum of integers is a HUGEINT.

Errors

Status Code When
400 parse_error The DSL does not parse
400 validation_error Semantic check failed
400 result_too_large An extract kv pipeline read more than max_export_rows input rows, or its aggregation would drop input at its group, distinct-value or exact-value cap. The message names the cap and its limit.
400 bad_request format is not csv, json, or parquet. The envelope’s message quotes the request’s reason.
500 execution_error DuckDB failed
503 query_resource_exhausted The export went over the spill or memory budget. See query resource exhausted.
503 service_unavailable The deadline passed before the export started
503 service_unavailable The hot buffer’s snapshot could not be built. The message is recent events could not be read for this query.
503 corpus_recovering The corpus is unsettled. See corpus recovering.
504 timeout The deadline passed after the export started

Captured results

Section titled “Captured results”

A capture runs one query once and keeps its result as an immutable, typed file that expires. Later reads page the stored rows and never run the query again. So row 7 of a capture is the same row a minute later, while new events keep arriving and compaction moves files. A captured row is the pair of a result id and a 0-based row number. It names a row of a frozen copy, not an event. ADR-0057 records the decision.

Three correlation reads build their own query from typed inputs and keep the answer as a capture too: the rows around a captured row, where a literal appears, and how one filter’s counts changed between two windows.

Every route in this section needs the query permission. A key reads only the captures it made: another key’s capture answers 404 not_found, as an unknown id does. The exception is kept evidence, which every key with investigation_read reads. The routes use the regular request count and the interactive rate limit. A page or cell read answers 400 bad_request to a query parameter it does not take, or to one that does not read as its type.

The numbers in this section are defaults. The [capture] table sets each of them.

Capture a result

Section titled “Capture a result”

POST /api/v1/results

Permission: query

Runs one query under every guard that run a query applies, and keeps its result: the key’s permission and rate, the request count, an executor permit, the publication guard, the query scratch budgets, history, and the query_timing event. A capture of the corpus answers 503 corpus_recovering while the corpus is unsettled. While it runs, the capture is listed by GET /api/v1/queries with the own flag, and as retained work with the kind capture when it outlives its request. Its history entry holds the executed text. It writes one query_timing event with the kind capture, which measures the file write in its own phase, query_write_us.

Parameters

Name In Type Required Description
query body string yes The DSL query
window body object no The time window, instead of time clauses in query. See bounds
window.earliest body string no The inclusive start, as an RFC 3339 instant such as 2026-10-23T09:00:00Z. An offset is applied
window.latest body string no The exclusive end, as an RFC 3339 instant
window.last body string no A span that ends now: a number and one of s, m, h, d, or w, such as 1h

The body and window refuse a member they do not know, so a misspelled window cannot capture the default window by accident.

Request

Response

The window matched 18,342 events. The capture kept the 5,000 most recent and says so in truncated.

A capture attached to an investigation (ADR-0059) also answers step_seq, an integer: the sequence of the step the capture appended to the investigation. An unattached capture’s answer has no step_seq.

Every capture, list, and page answer carries the result’s metadata in this shape:

Field Type Description
id string The result id: 32 lowercase hex digits, a random 128-bit value that is never reused
query string The query text as the caller sent it. For a correlation read, the text the server built
executed_query string The text that ran: the query with the resolved bounds spliced in and, for the events shape, the imposed sort -_time, -_ingested. A query of this text reads the same window
source string live for the corpus, read inside the bounds. stored for a from saved query, which reads a stored report run and has no bounds
shape string events or whole. See shapes and caps
earliest, latest string The resolved half-open window [earliest, latest), with microseconds. Absent for a stored source
created_at string When the result was committed
expires_at string When the result stops being readable: created_at plus [capture] ttl_secs (900). Absent for a kept result
state string temporary while it is readable. kept for kept evidence of an investigation. A gone result is expired or pruned
columns array The columns in stored positional order, each a result column with stored_as. Names are not unique
columns[].stored_as string native when the file stores the column in its own type. wire_text when no single file type holds it: a mixed column, or an integer column that holds both a negative value and one above 9223372036854775807. Reads answer both the same way
captured_rows integer Rows the file holds
total_rows integer Rows the executed query produced before the capture cut, exact, from the same execution
wire_bytes integer Bytes of the captured cells as the result columns encoding writes them, without framing. The byte cap counts this
file_bytes integer Bytes of the stored file. 0 for a result with no columns, which has no file. A correlation read’s correlation document is not counted here, but the quotas charge it with the file
truncated boolean true when captured_rows is less than total_rows
column_facts array Facts about each column over the captured rows, in the order of columns
column_facts[].nulls integer Captured rows whose cell is null
column_facts[].distinct integer Distinct non-null values, counted up to 6
column_facts[].distinct_capped boolean true when counting stopped at 6, so distinct is a lower bound
column_facts[].values array Each distinct value with its count, most frequent first. Present only when the column holds at most 5 distinct values and each value, as a tagged cell, is at most 256 bytes
column_facts[].min, column_facts[].max object The earliest and latest instant. Present for a _time column of type timestamp only, and absent when it holds an infinite or unordered instant
format_version integer The layout version of the stored file
kind string context, sightings, or compare for a correlation read. Absent for a capture made by this route
correlation object What a correlation read established, tagged with the same kind. Absent for a capture made by this route
investigation_id string The investigation that keeps the result. Present for a kept result, and for one whose retention as evidence ended

A fact value is a tagged cell, as a mixed column writes one: {"type": "integer", "value": "502"}. Text is tagged string whatever the column’s type, so a _time instant reads {"type": "string", "value": "..."}. The response’s execution has the meaning it has on run a query.

Bounds

Section titled “Bounds”

A live capture covers one window, which the server resolves once, at the instant T it reads its clock, in microseconds:

  • The window comes from one source: window, or the query’s own last=, earliest=, and latest=. A request with both is refused.
  • last=d covers [T − d, T).
  • earliest=X covers from X to latest=Y when given, and to T otherwise.
  • latest= alone is refused, because it names no start. Add earliest=, or give last= instead.
  • With neither, the capture covers the last 15 minutes, [capture] default_window_secs.
  • last beside earliest or latest is refused.
  • An empty window and a window longer than 7 days, [capture] max_span_secs, are refused.

In the query text, an earliest= or latest= value is read as run a query reads it, which drops a spelled offset, so write the instant in UTC. In window, an offset is applied. A value that names no finite instant is refused, and so is a value over 128 bytes, by its length alone. A refusal quotes at most 64 bytes of a value it names. A time clause must sit where the search takes it as the window: at the top level, under OR, inside parentheses, or directly under NOT. A clause inside NOT (...) filters nothing in a query, so a capture refuses it.

The server cuts the query’s own time clauses out of the text, writes the window in front as earliest="..." latest="..." with microseconds, and checks that the rest of the text is unchanged. The result is executed_query. A text where that check fails is refused with a request to write the time clause at the top level. Every refusal in this list is 400 bad_request, and comes before the capture takes anything.

A query whose first stage is from saved reads a stored report run, not the corpus. It takes no window and no time clause, and either is refused. It runs as written. Its result has source: "stored", no earliest or latest, and the whole shape.

Shapes and caps

Section titled “Shapes and caps”

A capture keeps at most 5,000 rows, [capture] max_rows, and at most 4 MiB of cells, [capture] max_wire_bytes. The byte cap counts each cell as the result columns encoding writes it, without the commas and brackets between cells. The engine’s own max_result_rows refusal applies first, with 400 result_too_large.

A result has the events shape when every stage after the search only filters events or adds fields: where, extract, let, drop, and rename, where no let, drop, or rename writes, removes, or renames _time or _ingested. The result must also carry both columns. The server appends | sort -_time, -_ingested to the executed text of every events capture, so the rows are newest first. That stage counts against the stage cap of 128, so the query of an events capture may carry at most 127 stages. A query with 128 is refused with 400 bad_request before the capture takes anything. When the rows pass a cap, the capture keeps the rows before the first one that does not fit, and total_rows counts every row. A first row larger than the byte cap leaves zero rows.

Every other result has the whole shape: one that aggregates, projects, orders, limits, deduplicates, or samples, such as stats, table, sort, head, top, or dedup, and every from saved result. A prefix of such a result answers a different question, so a whole result past either cap is refused with 400 result_too_large. The message names the cap and says to aggregate further or narrow the window.

A stored file larger than 8 MiB, [capture] max_file_bytes, is refused with result_too_large too. For a correlation read, the file and its correlation document together must fit that size.

A result with columns and no rows is stored as a file that holds only its columns. A result with no columns, such as a search that matches no event, has no file, and its file_bytes is 0.

Admission and quotas

Section titled “Admission and quotas”

A capture is admitted before it takes a query id, an executor permit, or the publication guard. A refusal leaves nothing taken, and the capture appears in neither /api/v1/queries nor history. It still writes one query_timing event with the kind capture. A bounds refusal has outcome=error and work_started=false, and carries query_dsl_check_us but no query_pool_wait_us. A refusal at the gates below has outcome=capacity_refused and work_started=false. The checks run in this order:

  1. The key’s quota, read ahead. A key that is already full is refused before it waits.
  2. The key’s lane. One capture per key runs at a time, [capture] per_key_running. Up to 4 more wait in the key’s queue, [capture] queue_depth, inside their own deadline. The next one is refused with 429 capture_busy.
  3. The installation. Two captures run at once, [capture] installation_running, inside the executor pool. A capture that finds both running is refused with 429 capture_busy. It does not queue.
  4. The binding reservation. The server first expires every temporary capture that is due and removes its file. It then reserves one result and 8 MiB, [capture] max_file_bytes, against the key’s quota and the installation’s quota, or refuses with 429 capture_quota_exceeded.

A capture’s stored bytes are its file and, for a correlation read, its correlation document as the server encoded it. The byte quotas count both.

Quota Key Default
Live captures per key per_key_results 64
Stored bytes per key per_key_bytes 64 MiB
Live captures per installation installation_results 512
Stored bytes per installation installation_bytes 512 MiB

A capture needs max_file_bytes of free quota to start, even when its file turns out small. When its row commits, the reservation becomes the real size of the file and its correlation document.

Both 429 answers carry Retry-After, in whole seconds and never less than 1. For capture_busy it is the time until the first running capture’s deadline. For capture_quota_exceeded it is the time until the first temporary result in the full quota expires, at most [capture] ttl_secs, and ttl_secs when none will expire. A capture whose deadline passes during admission, in the key’s queue or in the store calls that expire due captures and reserve quota, gets capture_busy with Retry-After: 1. A deadline that passes later is a 503 or a 504, as the outcomes table says.

A capture reads the stored files that a query of its recorded text reads. Before it scans, the server measures the files among them that can hold an event of the window, under the publication guard. A file is not counted when its footer statistics put every row group’s _time outside the window, because a sender’s clock can put an event’s time far from the hour it was stored. A file whose footer cannot show that for every row group, such as a file with a row group that has no _time statistics, is counted whole. A measure larger than 1 GiB, [capture] source_max_bytes, is refused with 400 capture_source_too_large. The message gives both byte counts and nothing else. The hot buffer is not counted. A from saved capture measures its run’s files against the same limit, and counts a missing file as 0 bytes.

A capture has one deadline of 15 seconds, [capture] deadline_secs, capped by [server] timeout_secs. It covers resolution, the wait in the queue, execution, and the file write. Past the deadline the capture ends as a query does. A client that disconnects cancels the work, as it cancels a query. The lane slot, the installation slot, and the reservation stay charged until the work has stopped.

A capture writes its file to the results root before it commits the result’s record, so a reader never finds a record whose file is still being written. The server commits the record even when the client has gone.

Errors

Status Code When
400 parse_error The query does not parse. The spans point into the text as sent
400 validation_error Unknown function, wrong arity, or a pipeline over the expression budget or stage cap
400 bad_request A bounds refusal: a window and a time clause together, latest= alone, an empty window, a span over max_span_secs, a value that names no instant, a time value over 128 bytes, a nested time clause, or a window or time clause on from saved. Also an events query of 128 stages, which leaves no stage for the imposed order
400 result_too_large The result exceeded max_result_rows, a whole result exceeded max_rows or max_wire_bytes, or the file exceeded max_file_bytes
400 capture_source_too_large The window, or the from saved run, selects more than source_max_bytes of stored data
400 execution_error A result cell is an integer outside the signed and unsigned 64-bit range
403 forbidden The key lacks query
404 not_found A from saved stage names a saved query the key does not own, or one with no successful run
409 bad_request A from saved stage selects a run that has columns but no Parquet file
429 capture_busy The key’s queue is full, two captures already run, or the deadline passed during admission: in the key’s queue, or in the store reads and writes that expire due captures and reserve quota. Sent with Retry-After, which is 1 for the deadline case
429 capture_quota_exceeded The key’s or the installation’s quota cannot take one more result. Sent with Retry-After
500 execution_error DuckDB failed or the capture was cancelled
503 query_resource_exhausted The query went over the spill or memory budget
503 service_unavailable The deadline passed after admission and before the work started: in the wait for an executor permit or the publication guard, or in the hand-off to the worker. The message is server at capacity: the query was not started. Nothing stays charged
503 service_unavailable The metadata store did not answer
503 corpus_recovering The corpus is unsettled. See corpus recovering
504 timeout The deadline passed after the work started, including while the file was being written. The work keeps its slots and its reservation until it stops, and a file it had not yet published is removed

List captured results

Section titled “List captured results”

GET /api/v1/results

Permission: query

Lists the key’s live captures, newest first: every temporary capture before its expires_at. A client that lost a capture’s response finds the result here. The list has no paging. It holds at most [capture] per_key_results entries.

Request

Response

Each entry has the fields of a captured result.

Errors

Status Code When
403 forbidden The key lacks query
503 service_unavailable The metadata store did not answer

Read a page of a captured result

Section titled “Read a page of a captured result”

GET /api/v1/results/{id}

Permission: query

Returns rows of a capture by row number, from the stored file. It runs no query and takes no executor permit.

Parameters

Name In Type Required Description
id path string yes The result id
offset query integer no The first row number, 0-based. Default 0. At most captured_rows; an offset equal to captured_rows is accepted and returns a page with no rows
limit query integer no Rows in the page. Default and cap: [capture] page_max_rows (200). 0 is accepted and returns a page with no rows
columns query string no Column names separated by commas. Default: every column

A name in columns selects every column with that name, so a duplicate name returns each of its columns. The page carries the selected columns in stored order, whatever order columns names them in. A name that the result does not have is 400 bad_request. An empty columns= names one column called '', so it is refused the same way unless the result has a column with an empty name. A name that holds a comma cannot be selected on its own; leave columns out to read every column.

Request

Response

Field Type Description
result object The captured result the page belongs to
positions array For each column of page, its 0-based position in result.columns, ascending
page object The selected columns and the page’s rows, encoded as result columns. Row i of the page is captured row offset + i
pagination.total integer The result’s captured_rows

A result with no columns answers rows that are empty arrays and reads no file. Two reads of the same rows of one capture return the same bytes, whatever ingest, compaction, or a restart did between them.

Errors

Status Code When
400 bad_request limit is above page_max_rows, offset is past captured_rows, columns names a column the result does not have, or a query parameter is unknown or not an integer
403 forbidden The key lacks query

Every captured result outcome applies too.

Read one cell of a captured result

Section titled “Read one cell of a captured result”

GET /api/v1/results/{id}/cells/{row}/{column}

Permission: query

Returns a byte range of one cell, so a client can read a cell too long for a page. The range is over the cell’s text as the result columns encoding writes it, under the column’s type. A string cell’s text is a JSON string, quotes included.

Parameters

Name In Type Required Description
id path string yes The result id
row path integer yes The row number, 0-based
column path integer yes The column’s position in columns, 0-based. Names are not unique, so a cell is addressed by position
offset query integer no The first byte of the range. Default 0. It must start a UTF-8 character: use 0 or a next_offset
length query integer no The most bytes in the range, at least 4. Default and cap: [capture] max_wire_bytes, which holds any captured cell whole

The range ends at a character boundary, so it can be shorter than length. Follow next_offset until it is absent, join the text values, and decode the joined text as a cell of the column’s type.

Request

Response

The next request asks for offset=64 and gets the rest of the cell, with no next_offset:

Field Type Description
type string The column’s type, spelled as a result column spells it. A list type also has items
offset integer The byte offset of text in the cell’s text
length integer The byte length of text
total_bytes integer The byte length of the whole cell’s text
next_offset integer The offset of the next range. Absent when text reaches the end
text string The range of the cell’s text

Errors

Status Code When
400 bad_request row is past the captured rows, column is past the columns, offset is past the cell or inside a character, length is below 4 or above max_wire_bytes, or a path segment or query parameter does not read as an integer
403 forbidden The key lacks query

Every captured result outcome applies too.

Correlation reads

Section titled “Correlation reads”

POST /api/v1/results/context, POST /api/v1/results/sightings, and POST /api/v1/results/compare each answer one question about the corpus and keep the answer as a capture. The server builds the query from the request’s typed fields. Each value sits in a quoted position, and the server parses the text back and checks that it reads as built, so a quote, a backslash, a pipe, or a comment opener in a value stays one value. The read then runs through the same steps as capture a result: the key’s permission and rate, the bounds, admission and quotas, the source budget, the deadline, cancellation when the client disconnects, and history. It writes one query_timing event whose kind is the read’s name: context, sightings, or compare. A read whose body names an investigation is attached to it as a search capture is: trawld records it as a step and keeps its result as evidence. See attach a capture. ADR-0058 records the decision.

The response has the shape of a capture response, result and execution. result.kind names the read. result.correlation holds what the read established, tagged with the same kind, and every later page and list entry of the capture carries the same object. result.query is the text the server built. executed_query is that text with the bounds spliced in, as for any capture. Read the rows with read a page.

Every refusal of the request itself comes before admission, so it takes no executor permit, no lane slot, and no quota. For an attached read it also comes before the step, so it records no step. That includes a refused field, a window longer than 7 days, overlapping windows, and a focus row the read cannot use. A window that selects more than [capture] source_max_bytes of stored data is refused with 400 capture_source_too_large before the scan, as for any capture.

The facts are bounded, because the server stores them beside the file and sends them with every answer about the capture:

  • sightings and compare list at most 5,000 groups. A read that finds more is refused with 400 result_too_large, and the message says what to change.
  • The correlation object, as the server encodes it, is at most 2 MiB. A larger one is refused with 400 result_too_large.
  • The object counts with the file against the key’s and the installation’s byte quotas, or, for an attached read, against the evidence budgets. The two together must fit [capture] max_file_bytes.

The statements write columns with ordinary names, because the DSL keeps names that begin with _ for trawl. sightings writes sighting_count, sighting_first, and sighting_last onto every match, over an event field of the same name. compare assigns compare_side, compare_fg, compare_bl, and its count, rate, change, and status columns, and refuses a group field with one of those names.

Every error of capture a result applies, with these additions:

Status Code When
400 bad_request A field is over its cap or is refused by name. The route sections list the cases
400 result_too_large More than 5,000 groups, or a correlation object over 2 MiB
400 focus_incomplete, focus_ambiguous Context only
400 windows_overlap Compare only
400 correlation_invalid An input the server cannot build into a query. The message names the input and quotes only the caller’s values
500 internal_error The server built a query that its own checks refuse. This is a server defect, not the caller’s
503 service_unavailable Compare only: the data directory’s environments could not be listed, so retention reach could not be checked. The message is environment listing failed

Read the rows around a captured row

Section titled “Read the rows around a captured row”

POST /api/v1/results/context

Permission: query

Reads the events around one row of a capture that the key holds, the focus row, and keeps them as a new capture. The read covers seconds on each side of the focus row’s _time, on the focus row’s own env and host, or on one of them as scope says. It answers three groups: the rows strictly earlier than the focus row’s _time, the rows at exactly that _time, and the rows strictly later.

Parameters

Name In Type Required Description
result_id body string yes The capture that holds the focus row
row body integer yes The focus row’s number, 0-based
scope body string no Which of the focus row’s keys hold the read: env_and_host, env, or host. Default env_and_host
seconds body integer no Seconds on each side of the focus row’s _time. Default 30
before body integer no The most rows strictly earlier than the focus row. Default 10, at most 50
after body integer no The most rows strictly later than the focus row. Default 10, at most 50
investigation body object no The investigation to attach the read to: id, and optionally seen_seq and purpose. See attach a capture

The body refuses a member it does not know.

The server reads the focus row as a page reads it, so another key’s temporary capture is not_found, an expired one is result_gone, and a key with investigation_read can focus on a row of kept evidence. An attached read keeps its own result and does not promote the focus capture. The focus capture can have any shape. The focus row must hold a timestamp in _time and a text value for each key that scope names. Otherwise the read is refused with focus_incomplete. It is never widened to more hosts or environments. A key that scope does not name is reported when the row holds it, and is not required.

The window is [_time − seconds, _time + seconds + 1 µs), so the focus instant is inside it. It must fit [capture] max_span_secs, as any capture window must. A window with more events than max_result_rows is refused with result_too_large. Make seconds smaller, or keep both keys in scope.

Of the events in the window, the capture keeps the before rows nearest before the focus instant, at most 20 rows at the focus instant, and the after rows nearest after it. The file stores them in that order, and each group is in ascending _time order. executed_query still ends with the imposed | sort -_time, -_ingested, because the server picks the groups from the rows in that order. The stored order is the group order. total_rows counts the rows the groups kept.

The focus row is not copied into the answer. The focus event is one of the rows at its _time, and it is not marked: this is a new read, and equal timestamps establish no order. Two identical events are two rows.

Request

Response

Ten rows came before the focus row, two shared its _time, and one came after it within 30 seconds.

Field Type Description
correlation.focus object The focus row as the request named it, with the time, env, and host the read took from it. env and host are null when the row holds no text value for them
correlation.scope_used object The env and host that held the read, null for a key that scope did not name, and the seconds
correlation.groups object earlier, same_time, and later, each a half-open range {start, end} of captured row numbers. An empty group has start equal to end
correlation.statement string Always new read; equal timestamps establish no order
step_seq integer Attached reads only. The seq of the step the read appended. See attach a capture
activity object Attached reads that sent seen_seq only. The entries other keys changed since then

Errors

Status Code When
400 bad_request before or after is above 50. The window has an instant outside the representable range, or is longer than max_span_secs
400 focus_incomplete row is past the capture’s rows. The focus row’s _time is missing, null, or not a timestamp. A key that scope names is missing, null, or not text
400 focus_ambiguous The focus capture has two columns named _time, or two named after a key that scope names
400 result_too_large The window holds more events than max_result_rows
403 forbidden Attached only: the key lacks investigation_read or investigation_write
404 not_found Attached only: no investigation has this id
409 investigation_closed Attached only: the investigation is closed
409 evidence_budget_exceeded Attached only: the investigation’s or the installation’s evidence budget cannot take the 8 MiB reservation
429 capture_busy Attached only: the key’s share of steps was full, or the deadline passed while the step waited for the database. Sent with Retry-After: 1

The focus capture’s outcomes apply too: 404, 409, 410, and 500.

Find where a literal appears

Section titled “Find where a literal appears”

POST /api/v1/results/sightings

Permission: query

Searches the window once for one literal, as a quoted text term: an event matches when its message or its _raw contains the literal, in any letter case. The read counts every match by env and service, with the first and last _time of each group, and keeps the 5,000 most recent matches as a capture. It then finds the fields that hold the literal in the kept matches.

Parameters

Name In Type Required Description
literal body string yes The text to find, such as an IP address. From 1 to 1024 bytes, with no NUL character
window body object no The bounds, in the shape of a capture’s window. Default: the last 24 hours. At most 7 days
fields body array no At most 16 field names to attribute the literal to. Default: every field
investigation body object no The investigation to attach the read to: id, and optionally seen_seq and purpose. See attach a capture

The body and window refuse a member they do not know.

The read has two populations, and denominators names both:

  • matches_total and groups count every match in the window, from the same execution, before the capture keeps the most recent 5,000. A group whose matches are all older than the kept rows still has its exact count and its first and last seen. service_counts_over is matches_total.
  • fields and raw_only_rows count the kept matches. field_counts_over is captured.

A field holds the literal when its cell’s text contains it, under the text search’s own rule. Text is itself. An integer is its decimal digits. A boolean is true or false. A float is its shortest decimal form, such as 12.5, 3 for 3.0, and 100000000000000000000 for 1e20, never an exponent. So the literal 3.0, copied from a float cell’s JSON, does not match that cell, whose text is 3. A timestamp is the text that the result writes. A null or a list cell holds nothing.

Attribution looks at every column except _raw and the three sighting_* columns. fields restricts which of those columns fields in the answer lists, and nothing else: the search, its matches, the groups, and raw_only_rows are the same with or without it. raw_only_rows counts the kept matches in which no column holds the literal, whatever fields says, so the literal matched through _raw alone. _raw can match field names and syntax, such as the key in {"status": 200}, so these matches are counted apart.

Every kept match carries its group’s sighting_count, sighting_first, and sighting_last. A window with more matches than max_result_rows is refused with result_too_large before anything is kept. Narrow the window or the literal.

Request

Response

The literal matched 7,214 events in three groups. The capture kept the 5,000 most recent. In 4,851 of them remote_addr holds it, and no kept match has src_ip. The 146 sshd matches hold it in message, so they are not raw-only, although fields does not name message. In three staging matches, remote_addr is a proxy and the literal is only in _raw.

Field Type Description
correlation.literal string The literal searched for
correlation.matches_total integer Every match in the window
correlation.captured integer The matches kept: the most recent ones, at most the capture’s cut
correlation.attribution_fields array The request’s fields as validated, in request order. Absent when the request named none. A field named here and absent from fields held the literal in no kept match
correlation.groups array One entry per (env, service) pair: its count, first_seen, and last_seen, exact over every match. Most matches first, then by service and env, with a null key last
correlation.fields array Each attributed field that holds the literal in at least one kept match, with the number of those matches as rows. Most rows first, then by name. At most 256
correlation.fields_omitted integer Attributed fields that hold the literal but are not in fields, because more than 256 do. Always 0 when the request names fields. The other counts are unaffected
correlation.raw_only_rows integer Kept matches in which no column but _raw holds the literal, over every column whatever fields says
correlation.denominators object field_counts_over, which is captured, and service_counts_over, which is matches_total
correlation.follow_ups array At most two DSL queries to run next: the literal on its busiest service, and its hourly count by service. They carry no time clause. Run them over the result’s earliest and latest
step_seq integer Attached reads only. The seq of the step the read appended. See attach a capture
activity object Attached reads that sent seen_seq only. The entries other keys changed since then

Errors

Status Code When
400 bad_request The literal is empty, holds a NUL character, or is over 1024 bytes. fields has more than 16 names, a name over 255 bytes, a name the DSL cannot write as a field, or one name twice under the field fold. A bounds refusal
400 bad_request fields names _raw, sighting_count, sighting_first, or sighting_last, in any letter case. The message is field "<name>" is reserved: attribution never counts `_raw` or the `sighting_count`, `sighting_first` and `sighting_last` columns the read writes
400 result_too_large More matches than max_result_rows, more than 5,000 groups, or a correlation object over 2 MiB. Narrow the window or the literal
403 forbidden Attached only: the key lacks investigation_read or investigation_write
404 not_found Attached only: no investigation has this id
409 investigation_closed Attached only: the investigation is closed
409 evidence_budget_exceeded Attached only: the investigation’s or the installation’s evidence budget cannot take the 8 MiB reservation
429 capture_busy Attached only: the key’s share of steps was full, or the deadline passed while the step waited for the database. Sent with Retry-After: 1

Compare two windows

Section titled “Compare two windows”

POST /api/v1/results/compare

Permission: query

Counts the events that one filter matches in a foreground window and in a baseline window, per group, in one statement, and keeps the ranked groups as a capture. The captured rows are the ranked table, so read a page returns it.

Parameters

Name In Type Required Description
filter body string yes DSL search terms, such as service=sshd "failed password". No pipe stage, and no time clause at any depth, under NOT or in parentheses included
foreground body object yes The window under question, in the shape of a capture’s window. {} is the last 15 minutes
baseline body object no The window to compare against, in the same shape. Default: the window of equal length that ends where foreground starts
group_by body array no At most 2 distinct field names. Default: none, so one row counts every event the filter matches
min_count body integer no A group is listed when either window counts at least this many events for it. Default 1
investigation body object no The investigation to attach the read to: id, and optionally seen_seq and purpose. See attach a capture

The body and both windows refuse a member they do not know.

Each window is half-open, [start, end), and is resolved as a capture window is. The windows can touch but not overlap. The capture covers their hull, from the earlier start to the later end, so the hull must also fit [capture] max_span_secs, and the source budget measures the hull.

The statement scans the hull once and labels each event with the window its _time falls in. It drops the events in neither window and counts each group in both windows at once. Both counts therefore come from one hot-buffer snapshot and one pin snapshot, and an event ingested while the statement runs counts in neither window. Two separate compare requests have no such promise: ingest, retention, or compaction can change the corpus between them.

Each captured row is one group, with these columns after the group fields:

Column Type Description
compare_foreground_count, compare_baseline_count integer Events in each window
compare_foreground_rate, compare_baseline_rate float Events per minute of each window. For a window of whole minutes, the count divided by its minutes. For any other, the count times 60,000,000 divided by its length in microseconds
compare_rate_change float compare_foreground_rate − compare_baseline_rate
compare_abs_rate_change float The absolute value of compare_rate_change
compare_relative_change float compare_rate_change / compare_baseline_rate, or null when the baseline count is 0
compare_status string new_in_foreground when the baseline count is 0, vanished when the foreground count is 0, and both otherwise

A group with no events in the baseline is new_in_foreground, never an infinite change. The rows are ranked by compare_abs_rate_change descending, then compare_foreground_count descending, then compare_baseline_count descending, then the group fields ascending, so the same request over the same data ranks the same. The result has the whole shape. Every column the statement assigns starts with compare_, so a user field such as status groups. A group field named after one of the columns above, such as compare_status, is refused, because the statement assigns that name before it groups.

Request

Response

The baseline defaulted to the hour before the foreground. A page of the result reads, in rank order, alice (30 failures against 6), dave (0 against 3, vanished), carol (2 against 0, new_in_foreground), and bob (5 against 5).

Field Type Description
correlation.foreground, correlation.baseline object Each resolved window: start (inclusive), end (exclusive), and duration_ms
correlation.group_by array The group fields
correlation.min_count integer The count a group reached in either window to be listed
correlation.rate_unit string Always per_minute
correlation.rows_ranked integer The groups listed, which are the captured rows. At most 5,000
correlation.warnings array What the read cannot vouch for, each with code, message, and field. At most four
step_seq integer Attached reads only. The seq of the step the read appended. See attach a capture
activity object Attached reads that sent seen_seq only. The entries other keys changed since then

A warning says the counts can be incomplete. No warning is a claim that they are complete. There are two codes:

  • retention_reach, with field null: a window starts before the oldest day that retention kept for an env that the filter selects, which is the env the filter names, or else every env on disk. There is at most one per window. It counts the envs that the window starts before, names at most eight of them in name order with the day each is kept from, counts the rest, and says data before the latest of those days may be missing. For example: the baseline window starts at 2026-10-16T00:00:00.000000Z, before the oldest day retention kept for 2 selected envs: prod (kept from 2026-10-17), staging (kept from 2026-10-18); data before 2026-10-18 may be missing. Storage names a partition by the day it was written, not by its events’ _time, so the warning claims nothing about the data after that day. It checks at most 1,024 selected envs. Past that, it adds retention reach was checked for the first 1024 of M selected environments, and it warns even when none of the checked envs is reached.
  • degraded_pin, with field naming the group field: the field’s pin is degraded, so events whose value was shelved count under a null value of the field. The server reads the degraded set that the schema refresh keeps, which can be up to one refresh old.

The retention check reads the data directory. A data directory or an environment directory that does not exist yet, below a directory that does, is a fresh start: it holds no data, so the check raises no warning for it. Any other directory that the check cannot list refuses the compare with 503 service_unavailable, because no warning could then say what was checked. A data directory, or an environment directory, that is a symlink to nothing, or sits below one, is such a case, not a fresh start. The compare is refused whether the filter names one env or not.

Errors

Status Code When
400 bad_request group_by has more than 2 names, a name over 255 bytes, or one name twice under the field fold. A window refusal: a window and its clauses mixed, latest alone, an empty window, a span or a hull over max_span_secs, an instant that does not parse, a value over 128 bytes
400 windows_overlap The windows overlap. The message names both as [start, end)
400 correlation_invalid The filter does not parse, has a pipe stage, or has a time clause. A group field is one of the statement’s columns or cannot be written as a field name. min_count is above 9223372036854775807. The filter’s text does not read back as written, such as a glob that holds a quote, so the read is refused rather than run as something else
400 result_too_large More than 5,000 ranked groups. Raise min_count or drop a group field
403 forbidden Attached only: the key lacks investigation_read or investigation_write
404 not_found Attached only: no investigation has this id
409 investigation_closed Attached only: the investigation is closed
409 evidence_budget_exceeded Attached only: the investigation’s or the installation’s evidence budget cannot take the 8 MiB reservation
429 capture_busy Attached only: the key’s share of steps was full, or the deadline passed while the step waited for the database. Sent with Retry-After: 1
503 service_unavailable The data directory’s environments could not be listed, so retention reach could not be checked. The message is environment listing failed

Captured result outcomes

Section titled “Captured result outcomes”

A page or cell read checks, in this order, before it reads any row:

Status Code When
404 not_found The id is not 32 lowercase hex digits, no capture has it, or another key made it and it is not kept evidence the key may read
410 result_gone The capture passed its expires_at, was pruned to fit a lowered quota, or its investigation’s evidence retention ended or the investigation was deleted. The message says which. The first two ask for a new capture; an ended retention says the findings that cite the result remain. Only the result’s owner gets the deleted-investigation answer; another key gets not_found
404 not_found The capture was gone for longer than [capture] tombstone_secs (86400), counted from the moment it was lost
409 result_unavailable The record exists, but its file is missing. The response is never an empty page, and the query is never run again
500 internal_error The record names a file format version that this server does not read
500 result_corrupt The file does not match the blake3 digest recorded at capture. The server checks the whole file on every read. The response names no path, and the server logs a result_corrupt event with the result id beside the request’s http_failure event
503 service_unavailable The metadata store did not answer

A gone capture keeps a record, called a tombstone, so that its owner can tell expired from never existed. A read that finds a temporary capture past its expires_at marks it expired and removes its file at once. The sweep removes the rest: every hour with the scheduler on, and every [capture] ttl_secs, at most hourly and at least every second, with it off. The sweep also deletes tombstones past tombstone_secs. A capture survives a restart until its expires_at. Back up and restore describes what the start does to captures and their files.

Investigations

Section titled “Investigations”

An investigation is a titled question that the installation keeps while an agent or a person works on it. It holds a log: the steps the server ran for it, the rows kept as evidence, findings, and notes. The installation owns it, not a key. Every key that holds query and investigation_read reads every investigation, so an agent and a person can work in the same one under different keys. ADR-0059 records the decision. The investigation tool of trawl mcp calls these routes.

Each route needs more than one permission:

Authority Permissions Routes
Read query and investigation_read List, read, and the kept evidence reads
Write Read, and investigation_write Create, append, overwrite, and attach a capture through POST /api/v1/results, /results/context, /results/sightings, or /results/compare
Manage Write, and server_manage Extend retention and delete

A key with server_manage alone cannot extend or delete: it needs the write permissions too. trawld checks the authority before it reads the path, the query string, or the body. So a key without it gets 403 forbidden for any request, and a key with it gets 400 bad_request for a request that does not read as its type. Attach a capture is the exception. Its four routes, POST /api/v1/results, /results/context, /results/sightings, and /results/compare, need query, and trawld checks query before it reads the body. Only the body says that a capture names an investigation, so trawld checks Write authority after it reads the body and before it writes anything. A key with query but without Write authority gets 400 bad_request for a body that does not read as the route’s request, and 403 forbidden for one that does. Any writer can close or reopen any investigation. The creator’s identity is attribution and grants nothing.

The routes use the regular request count and the interactive rate limit. Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC with microseconds.
